key_insight: Biologically guided tumor microenvironment transcriptomic features predicted immunotherapy response better and more consistently than data-driven gene selection in advanced urothelial carcinoma.
clinical_relevance: Transcriptomic profiling may add meaningful response-prediction value, but its benefit is modest once standard and research biomarkers are already included.
method: Compared knowledge-guided gene-set features with transcriptome-wide gene selection.
Evaluated incremental predictive value over clinical variables, standard biomarkers, and research-enriched biomarkers.
Assessed stability across cross-validation folds and external validation.
evidence_signal: In IMvigor210 (n=298), knowledge-guided features improved AUPRC by 0.058 over clinical variables alone, with smaller gains over biomarker-rich baselines; external evaluation showed the same pattern.
watch_item: Data-driven gene selection was unstable across folds, so results may not generalize well without biologically informed feature design.
paper_title: Incremental Predictive Value and Representation of Transcriptomic Features for Immunotherapy Response in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
